subsystems.role: the mathematical foundation: finding the shortest vector in a very high-dimensional lattice is believed hard even for quantum computers.

subsystems.role: lets two parties agree on a shared secret over a public channel.

subsystems.name: Arithmetic engine
subsystems.role: makes lattice maths fast and safe enough to run at network speed.

buildSteps.title: Pick a hard problem
buildSteps.detail: Designers base security on worst-case lattice problems such as Learning With Errors, so that breaking any key implies solving a very hard geometric problem in high dimension.

buildSteps.title: Choose parameters
buildSteps.detail: Dimension, modulus and error width are tuned so that known attacks — lattice reduction, sieving — need implausible time, while keys and ciphertexts stay small enough for real networks.

buildSteps.title: Design the scheme
buildSteps.detail: A public key is built from noisy linear equations; recovering the secret requires removing the noise. Signatures use a commitment, a hashed challenge and a response that only works if the signer knows a short lattice vector. Rejections throw away outputs that would leak the secret.

buildSteps.title: Standardise
buildSteps.detail: Candidates were publicly broken, compared and refined over several years, then frozen in published standards so independent implementations interoperate.

buildSteps.title: Implement in software
buildSteps.detail: Engineers write polynomial arithmetic, sampling and encoding in constant time, vectorised with SIMD instructions, avoiding branches or memory access patterns that vary with secret data.

buildSteps.title: Validate and attack
buildSteps.detail: Known-answer tests, formal verification, fault-injection and timing attacks are run against implementations before they are trusted with real traffic.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and migrate
buildSteps.detail: Libraries are linked into TLS, SSH and VPN stacks, often running the new algorithm alongside a classical one so that a break in either alone does not expose the session.

buildSteps.title: Roll out through updates
buildSteps.detail: Because it is software, deployment happens through ordinary patches to browsers, servers, phones and hardware security modules — the hard part is inventorying everything that needs updating.

pathway.milestone: lattice standards published and hybrid key exchange already shipping in major browsers and messaging apps
pathway.unlocks: protection against traffic recorded today and decrypted later.

pathway.milestone: hybrid signatures and certificates across web PKI, VPNs and code signing
pathway.unlocks: authentication that survives a future quantum break, not just confidentiality.

pathway.milestone: hardware security modules, smart cards and embedded devices gain lattice support
pathway.unlocks: migration of the long-lived, hard-to-update equipment that banks and governments depend on.

pathway.milestone: classical-only key exchange retired, with crypto-agility designed in from the start
pathway.unlocks: systems that can swap algorithms again quickly if lattice schemes are ever weakened.
